key_insight: An agentic AI workflow links liver lesion segmentation to structured radiology reports grounded in traceable, computed measurements.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help translate imaging predictions into interpretable reports while preserving links to quantitative evidence.
method: TotalSegmentator-based nnU-Net models segment the liver, Couinaud segments, and lesions.
Computational tools calculate volumes, dimensions, lesion counts, and anatomical locations.
An LLM organizes measurements into a predefined report schema, with numerical consistency checks.
evidence_signal: On 51 LiTS cases, segmentation achieved liver Dice 0.947, lesion sensitivity 75.6%, and positive predictive value 68.9%; separate exploratory screening identified liver-related abnormalities in 10,208 of 25,494 MERLIN reports (40.0%).
watch_item: The abstract does not establish clinical reporting accuracy or workflow benefit, and segmentation errors could propagate into reports.
paper_title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Liver Lesion Segmentation and Structured Radiology Reporting
